blocks.prompt: 3. A parabolic arch has 120 m base and height 25 m. Find the height of the arch at a point 42 m from the centre of the base.
blocks.explanation:
An arch is a parabola that opens downward.
Given: base 120 m, height 25 m. To find: the height of the arch above a point 42 m from the centre.
Plan: vertex at the origin, \(x^2 = -4ay\); an end of the base gives \(4a\); then put \(x = 42\).
steps:
Given: base 120 m, height 25 m.
To find: the height of the arch 42 m from the centre of the base.
Method: put the origin at the top (vertex) of the arch, \(y\)-axis vertical. The arch opens downward, so take \(x^2 = -4ay\).

An end of the base
The ends of the base are 60 m on each side of the centre and 25 m below the top:
\[A(60,\ -25)\]
Why: half of 120 is 60, and the base is 25 m below the vertex.

Find \(4a\)
\[60^2 = -4a(-25)\]
\[3600 = 100a \Rightarrow a = 36\]
\[4a = 144,\quad x^2 = -144y\]
Why: \(A\) lies on the arch.

Point 42 m from the centre
\[42^2 = -144y\]
\[y = -\dfrac{1764}{144} = -12.25\]
Why: \(y\) is measured from the top, so this point of the arch is 12.25 m below the top.

Height above the base
\[25 - 12.25 = 12.75 \text{ m}\]
Why: the top is 25 m above the base; the arch at this point is 12.25 m lower than the top.

Check
\[y = 25\left(1 - \dfrac{42^2}{60^2}\right) = 25(1 - 0.49)\]
\[= 12.75\]
Why: with the origin at the centre of the base the arch is \(y = 25\left(1 - \frac{x^2}{3600}\right)\); same answer.
